tasks.title: Derivar development.sequence da mesma resolução que já produz development.workflow_version, usando SEQUENCE_BY_VERSION
tasks.note: Em state_template() (grill_workspace.py), logo após `value['development']['workflow_version'] = resolved_version` (resolved_version substitui a expressão inline anterior 'v3' if sole == 'v2' else sole, agora nomeada e reaproveitada): `value['development']['sequence'] = list(SEQUENCE_BY_VERSION[resolved_version])`. SEQUENCE_BY_VERSION é o mesmo dicionário module-level que development_sequence() usa no lado do auditor (linha ~2241), então um bundle materializado aqui já concorda por construção com o que o auditor recomputa a partir de workflow_version sozinho -- não há dois caminhos de derivação para o mesmo fato. Comentário adicionado explica por que os dois campos (workflow_version e sequence) têm de derivar juntos: são a mesma informação (qual sequência de etapas este bundle fala), e deixar sequence vindo do asset (sempre a tupla da versão ativa) enquanto workflow_version é derivado produz o estado contraditório que validate_checkpoint_contract.py reprovava como DEVELOPMENT-SCHEMA. O comentário pré-existente que justifica a equivalência v2->v3 (SEQUENCE_BY_VERSION não tem entrada 'v2'; audit_decisions.WORKFLOW_SEQUENCE_BY_MARKER prova que v2 e v3 declaram a mesma tupla de onze etapas) foi mantido intacto.

part_1_desalt_eight_tests.finding: None of the eight named tests (test_one_item_top_level_and_item_schema, test_markdown_in_progress_stage_is_named, test_markdown_omits_closed_items_and_reports_pending_stage, test_markdown_terminal_contradiction_is_blocked, test_drift_is_silent_on_the_recorded_branch_however_many_commits, test_both_heads_stay_visible_for_whoever_needs_the_difference, test_specify_checkpoint_binds_phase_branch_and_status_exposes_it, and the T015 test test_status_projects_bundle_created_over_v3_document_by_the_v3_sequence) contains a literal hardcoded v4 step-name tuple. Verified by grep: the only 'partition'/'implement-parallel'/'agent-assign'/'agent-execute' literals in tests/validate_status_contract.py are the deliberate v3 hardcodes the brief said not to touch (_to_v3 helper and the T015 fixture-based test's own v3_sequence local, which already derives correctly). Their assumption of v4 was implicit: they relied on grill_status.py silently judging every bundle against SEQUENCE (v4) regardless of what development.sequence the bundle itself declared. All eight passed unmodified once that silent default was removed and item_payload/classify_item were fixed to project a tracked bundle strictly against its OWN development.sequence.

No assertion in any of the eight tests was changed.
part_1_desalt_eight_tests.lines_explicitly_not_touched: Deliberate v3 hardcodes building explicit v3 bundles (the _to_v3 helper and the two tests that use it, plus the T015 fixture test's own v3_sequence local) -- left exactly as found.

part_2_production_fallback.removed: Module-level SEQUENCE = [...] (the v4 tuple, formerly line 24) -- deleted after confirming (grep) it had no remaining reference anywhere in the file once its three call sites were fixed.
call_sites_fixed: item_payload(): the 'legacy-untracked' (dev is None) and 'invalid' (schema check failed) branches formerly set item_sequence = SEQUENCE. Changed to item_sequence = [] -- absence is treated as absence, never as the active version's tuple.

item_payload(): next_gate computation formerly fell back to "complete" whenever len(completed) was not < len(item_sequence); with item_sequence now legitimately empty for the two branches above, that produced a false "complete" for an untracked/invalid item. Guarded it: falls back to "complete" only when tracking == "tracked" (the one case item_sequence is guaranteed non-empty), otherwise "unknown".

classify_item(): the sequence=None default fallback formerly read `sequence = SEQUENCE if sequence is None else sequence`. Changed to `sequence = [] if sequence is None else sequence`, with a docstring paragraph naming the constitutional clause.
part_2_production_fallback.companion_fix_required_to_actually_pass_: Removing the SEQUENCE fallback alone did not make the eight tests pass: a freshly-created item (WORKFLOW.md defaults to v2, which resolves to v3) declares development.sequence correctly as the v3 tuple (agent-assign/agent-execute), but development.steps is still populated straight from assets/state.template.json's raw v4-shaped dict (grill_workspace.py's state_template() only overrides development.workflow_version and development.sequence, never development.steps -- out of this task's grant, in plugin/skills/grill-with-docs/scripts/grill_workspace.py, not grill_status.py). That leaves a consistent, correctly-declared v3 item with a steps dict missing the v3-only keys (agent-assign, agent-execute), which item_payload's own INVALID-DEVELOPMENT-SEQUENCE check (steps.get(s) not in STATES for s in item_sequence) flagged as corruption purely because the key was ABSENT, not because any present value was wrong. Fixed by treating an absent step key, for a step named in the item's OWN already-verified-consistent sequence, as implicitly 'pending' (steps.get(s, "pending") in place of steps.get(s), applied uniformly in item_payload's completed/blocked/findings computation and in classify_item's all_steps_complete/in_progress/pending loops). This never marks anything falsely complete (only 'pending' is ever supplied for an absence) and still flags a step that IS present with a disallowed value, or completed out of order, exactly as before.
part_2_production_fallback.residual_known_gap_out_of_grant: grill_workspace.py's state_template() not deriving development.steps from the same resolved version as development.sequence/workflow_version is a real production inconsistency, left as-is because grill_workspace.py is not in this task's grant. grill_status.py now tolerates it defensively (absence -> pending) rather than propagating it as a false BLOCKED verdict.
